name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,453

clue.text: Kick heading over rugby posts perhaps for ticket office

blocks.note: to kick something is to give it a boot
rugby goalposts are shaped like this capital letter

explanation.surface: A rugby kicker sends the ball over the posts, oddly heading for the ticket office.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, BOOT sits above, or heads over, the H. 'Perhaps' warns that the posts are only an example of the letter's shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth is a small enclosed kiosk where tickets are sold, as at a box office or fairground.

clue.text: Do karaoke? Why not in undergarments!

blocks.note: karaoke is singing along to backing tracks
'Why not?' as an eager suggestion means 'Let's!'

explanation.surface: Someone urges a karaoke session performed in nothing but underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Singlets are sleeveless vests worn under shirts, so they count as underclothing.

clue.text: Right to stop accepting wrong?

indicators.note: a word that accepts something takes it inside itself, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to deter is to stop or discourage
a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.surface: A moral question: is it right to prevent people taking up wrongdoing?
explanation.walkthrough: DETER takes in X to give DEXTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic and formal word for the right-hand side, as opposed to sinister on the left.

clue.text: Cultivate soft, hairy plant

indicators.note: cultivating land works and turns it over, so these letters are dug into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardening instruction to grow some downy, fuzzy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub with bright yellow spring flowers, a common garden species.

clue.text: Harass one who's in vehicle going downhill?

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, to taunt the batsman who is in at the crease
second meaning: a runnered conveyance for sliding down snowy slopes

explanation.surface: Bullying someone riding a toboggan down a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsman currently batting is 'in', and fielders who verbally needle them are said to sledge; the surface makes 'one who's in' a passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledging is cricket slang for taunting an opponent, and a sledge is also a toboggan that runs down snowy slopes.

clue.text: Amazeballs? The reverse!

indicators.note: the reverse of something faces the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: nuts is slang for testicles

explanation.surface: A mock exclamation using the slang word for amazing, then saying the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the slang word into 'Amaze' and 'balls': the word meaning amaze is the reverse of a word for balls, so STUN backwards gives NUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or stupefy them, the same as to amaze them.

clue.text: Goody-goody interrupting, I suppose

indicators.note: a word that interrupts breaks into the middle of another, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: pi, short for pious, describes a sanctimonious goody-goody
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A prig cuts in with a hesitant 'I suppose'.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is the crossword's usual goody-goody; 'I' looks like the speaker but is the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, much as to suppose is to hold a belief or view.

clue.text: Can US city with eyesore on outskirts see arterial congestion as a result of it?

indicators.note: something on the outskirts lies around the edges, so it wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: the can is slang for the toilet
Washington DC
a blot on the landscape is an eyesore

explanation.surface: A traffic report asks whether an ugly American city will see its main roads jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial' suggests main roads; here it means blood vessels, and 'see ... as a result of it?' hints at what the congestion produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood clot blocks an artery, which is literally a congestion in the arterial system.

clue.text: Carbon dioxide's attraction

indicators.note: read as 'has', the phrase before it holds the answer within its letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on what holds the atoms of a familiar gas together.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: carbon dioxide's atoms really are held by chemical bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a tie or force of attachment between people or atoms, so it can mean attraction.

clue.text: Calls on to abandon evil

blocks.note: to drop something is to give it up
a sin is an evil act

explanation.surface: A preacher calls on the congregation to forsake wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in on someone is to pay them a casual visit, which is to call on them.

clue.text: Tense rowing team losing lead, caught by one having two extra crew?

indicators.note: losing its lead means the word drops its first letter
something caught by another is held inside it

blocks.note: a racing eight is a crew of eight rowers
an eight plus two more makes this number

explanation.surface: A nervous rowing team loses its leader and is overtaken by a bigger boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A racing eight with two extra crew is a playful cryptic way to reach the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense muscles is to tighten them, so the two verbs share the sense of making taut.

clue.text: What's the point in pig put on mountain?

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: north, a compass point
a sow is a female pig
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A grumpy question about the purpose of hauling a pig up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Snowdon is the highest mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdon is the tallest peak in Wales, so it is a specific example of a mountain.

clue.text: Strange dam on Dee

blocks.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
Dee is the spelt-out name of the letter

explanation.surface: An odd barrage built across the River Dee.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a real river in Britain, which makes the dam plausible, but here it is just the letter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird and strange are close synonyms, both meaning odd or uncanny.

clue.text: Samples plant in back street

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
going back means the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation for street
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Instructions to put trial plants in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back street' looks like a single phrase, but 'back' acts on the street abbreviation alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasters are small portions offered for trying, so they are samples of food or drink.

clue.text: Place where what's seen is heard

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a sight is something seen

explanation.surface: A riddle about a place where you can hear what you see.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or plot of ground, so it means a place.

clue.text: Cosmetic I extracted from fish raised on lake

indicators.note: something extracted is taken out, so that letter is removed
in a down answer, raising a word reads it upwards, so in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written: the letter removed
a hoki is a hake-like fish of New Zealand waters
the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A make-up item, the narrator says, was pulled from a fish hauled up from a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: HOKI without its I is HOK, which reads upward as KOH; then L.
explanation.definitionFit: Kohl is a black powder used as eyeliner, a traditional cosmetic in many cultures.

clue.text: Risks a wet upset?

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and jumbled, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes the chance of a soaking tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: these planks invite a wet tumble into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterskis are the boards towed behind a boat, and anyone using them risks falling into the water.

clue.text: Unfolding vista - troops, be on lookout

indicators.note: unfolding opens out and rearranges, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: As the view opens up, soldiers are told to keep watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a military position from which to watch the enemy, a lookout point.

clue.text: Ruled on corrupt ring

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so these letters are distorted into another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge has issued a ruling on a crooked gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a criminal syndicate; here it is a circular shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a circular disc or emblem, such as the RAF marking, so it is a ring shape.

clue.text: Love to write and sing chaotic overtures

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters before it are jumbled

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like this letter
to pen is to write
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer loves to write and sing wild orchestral introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overtures' looks musical, matching the surface; here it means first approaches or starts.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtures are opening moves or introductory pieces, so both senses match beginnings.

clue.text: Devilled cutlet with 'reduction' of endive leaves

indicators.note: devilled food is spiced up, so the word beside it is cooked into a new order
a reduction boils something down, here to just its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A menu description: spicy cutlet served with a sauce reduction and endive salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduction' is in quotes because it is the cooking term borrowed to mean cut down to one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a salad plant eaten as its green leaves, so the leaves stand for the whole plant.

clue.text: Go to put one pound in hat

indicators.note: putting something in another places it inside

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a try
Roman numeral one
the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: An instruction to drop a pound coin into a hat, like a busker's collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One pound' looks like a single coin, but it splits into the numeral and the weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown and narrow brim.

clue.text: Farewell all, distinguished individuals exiting -  universally prominent characters

indicators.note: the most prominent characters stand at the front, so only each word's leading letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
first letter of the word
first letter of the word
first letter of the word
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A grand goodbye to all the notable people leaving, famous figures everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye used in English, a parting word meaning farewell.

clue.text: It's used in game theory

blocks.note: surface reading: the mathematical study of strategic decisions
setter's reading: a tile used in a tabletop game, and also the name of a Cold War theory about falling nations

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game theory' is a single academic term, but split it: the piece is used in a game, and its name labels the theory that one country falling to communism topples its neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a playing tile in the game of dominoes, and the domino theory is a famous political idea.

clue.text: Martial artist, having gained weight, to start getting lighter

indicators.note: having gained something means taking it in, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: a dan is a graded expert in judo or karate
the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A fighter who has put on weight is about to start slimming down.
explanation.walkthrough: W goes inside DAN. 'Getting lighter' looks like losing weight; it means the sky brightening.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawn is for daylight to begin, so it means the sky starting to become brighter.

clue.text: Mean cutie runs away

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: 'my pretty' is an endearment for an attractive person
the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An unkind sweetheart flees.
explanation.walkthrough: PRETTY loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means small-minded and spiteful, which is the unkind sense of mean.

clue.text: They may be shaped using basins or a dish, badly

definitions.text: They may be shaped using basins

indicators.note: something done badly comes out wrong, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen talk about shaping something in a bowl or a poorly made dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' belongs to the fodder rather than linking. A pudding-basin cut is made by trimming round a bowl placed on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdos are styled haircuts, and the bowl cut is literally shaped round a basin.

clue.text: Injure end of finger in chalet

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a chalet is a wooden hut
last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone hurts a fingertip in a ski lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside HUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt someone is to cause them injury, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: More air needs to circulate in cupboard

indicators.note: circulating things move round and change places, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that a stuffy wardrobe needs better ventilation.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoire is a tall freestanding wardrobe, a type of cupboard for clothes.

clue.text: Craft beer turning bad - atmospheric gases rising

definitions.text: Craft beer turning bad - atmospheric gases rising

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion, so the next word is shaped into a new arrangement
turning round makes the following word face the other way
in an across answer, rising means the letters before it are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
ill means bad, as in ill will
nitrogen and oxygen, the main gases of air, by their chemical symbols

explanation.surface: An ale goes off as the gases build up in the cask.
explanation.walkthrough: Rebellion is a craft brewery in Marlow, so the whole clue also describes its beer turning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a real English craft beer, and the description of fermentation gone wrong fits a revolt against authority.

clue.text: Nearly time when one retires?

blocks.note: nigh means nearly, as in well nigh
the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is almost the hour for retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retires' looks like leaving work for good; it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire can mean to go to bed, which most people do at the dark end of the day.
